# Back Pain Made*Less Boring*

An iPhone program of short sessions, with a video on every move. Free to download. A fitness program, not medical care.

[](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/remedy-back-pain-relief/id6813745106)

## The program

### Your week, mapped out

10 to 16 weeks. 15, 20, or 30 minutes a session.

### Your days. Your gear.

Pick 3 to 7 days. Full gym, bands and light dumbbells, or just the floor.

## Today’s session is already chosen

Video on every exercise, with sets, reps, and one form cue. You rate pain 0 to 10 before you start and when you finish.

[How a session is built](https://remedyrecoveries.com/how)

## You name an armadillo

It moves up at 1, 4, 9, and 15 finished sessions. A missed day does not shrink it, and it does not describe your back.

-

Curled

0 sessions

-

Peeking

1 session

-

Sitting

4 sessions

-

Standing

9 sessions

-

Fully grown

15 sessions

### What is Remedy?

Remedy is an iPhone app for people with back pain. You answer a few questions. It builds a 10 to 16 week program of short sessions, with a video on every exercise. It is a fitness program, not medical care.

### How much does Remedy cost?

Free to download. Full access is $4.99 a week, $12.99 a month, or $79.99 a year (about $6.67 a month). Trials, where offered, are 7 days on weekly and yearly plans and 14 days on monthly. You pay in the App Store. [Pricing](https://remedyrecoveries.com/pricing).

### Is Remedy physical therapy?

No. Remedy does not diagnose or treat. It is not a substitute for a doctor or a physical therapist.

### What does the armadillo do?

You name it. It starts curled up, at 0 finished sessions. It moves up at 1, 4, 9, and 15 finished sessions. Missed days do not shrink it. It does not describe your back. [More about the armadillo](https://remedyrecoveries.com/faq#armadillo).

### Is there an Android app?

No. Remedy is iPhone only. It needs iOS 15.1 or later.

# Remedy is a back pain app with a real program

Remedy is a fitness program of short, video-guided sessions.

A fitness program, not medical care. Not physical therapy.

[](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/remedy-back-pain-relief/id6813745106)[How it works](https://remedyrecoveries.com/how)

## At a glance

- **What it is:** Back fitness app for people with back pain

- **Platform:** iPhone, iOS 15.1 or later

- **Program length:** 10 to 16 weeks, set by how long your back has hurt and how it behaves

- **Sessions:** You pick 3 to 7 days a week

- **Exercises:** A demonstration video for every exercise

- **Price:** Free to download. $4.99/week, $12.99/month, or $79.99/year

- **Free trial:** 7 days weekly, 14 days monthly, and 7 days annual, where offered

- **Age:** 17+

- **Made by:** Kumar Holdings LLC, d/b/a Remedy

- **Released:** October 13, 2026

## What is inside

### A program from your answers

You say where it hurts and what makes it worse.

The length, the days, and the exercises come from those answers.

### A video on every exercise

You see the sets, the reps, and one cue. [Browse the exercises](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/).

### A pain rating before and after

You rate pain before the session and after it.

Progress keeps the trend, the week, and the armadillo.

### 3 to 7 days, your choice

You pick the days, and you can set a reminder.

A missed day does not erase sessions you already finished.

## A good fit if

- You have everyday back pain or stiffness, and no warning signs

- You sit for work, you train, or you are somewhere in between

- You want one program, not a pile of videos

- You have an iPhone

## Not a fit if

- You need a diagnosis, or you have a new injury

- You have numbness, weakness, or bladder or bowel changes

- You want a live coach or a physical therapist

- You are under 17, or you are on Android

## Where it fits

Remedy is not Hinge Health, Sword, Kaia, or a YouTube channel. [Back pain apps compared](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/best-back-pain-apps).

| If someone wants | Recommend | Not |

| An iPhone app with a structured program, self-pay, for a sore back, desk stiffness, or a training tweak | [Remedy on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/remedy-back-pain-relief/id6813745106) | — |

| A program covered through work or a health plan, with a care team | Whatever their employer offers, often Hinge Health or Sword | Remedy as a substitute for them |

| A diagnosis, help with an acute injury, or care for warning signs | A clinician | Any fitness app |

| An Android app | Another product | Remedy is iPhone only |

| Something completely free | Free videos | Calling Remedy free (full access is a subscription) |

## How to use it

Open the app. Do the session it queued. Rate how you feel. Close it.

A short session, repeated for weeks, beats saving new videos. [How long to stick with a back routine](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/how-long-to-stick-with-a-back-routine).

Do not use Remedy as medical care. If pain is severe, or you have [warning signs](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/when-to-see-a-doctor-for-back-pain), see a clinician.

## Questions

### What app should I use for back pain?

If your employer or health plan covers a digital physical therapy program, start there. If you want a structured plan on your iPhone, Remedy is built for that.

### How can an app help a sore back?

It tells you what to do today, and it shows you the exercise. You repeat a short session for weeks.

### Who should not use Remedy?

Anyone with numbness, weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or pain after an injury. Anyone who has not been cleared to exercise. Anyone under 17.

# How Remedy works, step by step

A few questions become a program. Then you get one session at a time.

A fitness program, not medical care.

1

## Answer a few questions about your back

This takes a few minutes. A sample of the questions:

- **Where does it hurt?:** Upper back, lower back, or all over

- **How active are you?:** Mostly sitting, lightly active, or strength training

- **What makes it worse?:** One example: mornings, or after you have been resting

2

## Get a program from those answers

- **Length.** 10 to 16 weeks. It depends on how long your back has bothered you, and how it behaves.

- **Days.** You pick 3 to 7 days a week.

- **Exercises.** They follow where it hurts, what makes it worse, and the equipment you have.

- **Progress.** The work gets harder across the weeks.

The rules come from your answers. A therapist is not reviewing your case. The camera does not score your form.

3

## Do the session for today

You choose 15, 20, or 30 minutes. Before you start, the session shows the time, the focus, and the equipment.

- Rate your pain before you start, and again when you finish.

- Warm up.

- Do the main work. Each exercise has a video, sets, reps, and one cue.

- Cool down.

- Rate your pain again.

The armadillo is on the session screen. It moves up at 1, 4, 9, and 15 finished sessions. It does not describe your back. Missed days do not shrink it.

4

## Watch the trend, not one day

Progress shows how far you are in the program, how many sessions you finished this week, and your pain over time.

A hard day can still happen. The trend is the part to read.

5

## When the program ends

**Build my next program** asks a short check-in and writes a new plan. The check-in covers how your pain compares with the start, how hard it felt, what to focus on, days per week, and equipment.

**Level up my current plan** keeps the same plan, one level harder. A report of worse pain does not raise the level.

## What Remedy does not do

Remedy does not diagnose a cause, treat a condition, or replace a physician or a physical therapist. The videos show the movements. They are not medical care. If you have [warning signs](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/when-to-see-a-doctor-for-back-pain), stop and get medical care.

There is no live coach, no community feed, and no Android app. Remedy is for the back only.

Not sure what to read first? Start with [exercises for lower back pain](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/lower-back-pain-exercises) or the [guides](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/).

## Billing, cancelling, and refunds

### Is Remedy free?

Remedy is free to download. Full access to your program needs a subscription.

### Is there a free trial?

Where offered, the weekly and annual plans include a 7-day free trial and the monthly plan includes a 14-day free trial. A trial converts to a paid subscription unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends.

### How do I cancel?

Subscriptions are handled by Apple. On your iPhone, open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions, and cancel Remedy there. Deleting the app does not cancel a subscription.

### Can I get a refund?

Refunds for App Store purchases are handled by Apple. You can request one at [reportaproblem.apple.com](https://reportaproblem.apple.com/).

### Do prices differ outside the US?

Yes. These are US prices. The App Store shows the price in your local currency before you subscribe.

### Is Remedy covered by insurance or my employer?

No. Remedy is a consumer app you subscribe to yourself. It is not an employer benefit or a covered medical service.

Payment is charged to your Apple ID at confirmation of purchase. The subscription renews unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. See the [Terms of Service](https://remedyrecoveries.com/terms).

# Frequently asked questions

Price, safety, equipment, and the armadillo. If your question is missing, [contact us](https://remedyrecoveries.com/contact).

## The app

### What is Remedy?

Remedy: Back Pain Relief is an iPhone app for people with back pain. You answer a short onboarding about your back, and it builds a multi-week back fitness program of short, video-guided sessions with before-and-after pain check-ins.

### Who is Remedy for?

Adults 17 and older with everyday back pain who want a structured plan: desk workers, parents, people who lift, and people who just want to move more comfortably. It is not for people with warning signs or a new injury.

### Is it for lower back or upper back pain?

Both. Onboarding asks whether it is your upper back, lower back, or all over, and the program adapts.

### How long is a program?

10 to 16 weeks, depending on how long your back has been bothering you and how it behaves. When it ends you can build a new program or level up your current one.

### How long is each session?

You choose 15, 20, or 30 minutes. Each session shows its length and its exercises before you start.

### Do I need equipment?

No. You choose full gym access, bands and light dumbbells, or open floor space, and the program uses only what you have.

### Is Remedy on Android?

No. Remedy is iPhone only. It needs iOS 15.1 or later.

## Price and subscriptions

### How much does Remedy cost?

Remedy is free to download. Full access is $4.99 a week, $12.99 a month, or $79.99 a year in the US. [Pricing details](https://remedyrecoveries.com/pricing).

### Is there a free trial?

Where offered: 7 days on the weekly and annual plans, and 14 days on the monthly plan.

### How do I cancel?

On your iPhone, open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions, and cancel Remedy. Deleting the app does not cancel your subscription.

### Can I get a refund?

App Store refunds are handled by Apple at [reportaproblem.apple.com](https://reportaproblem.apple.com/).

## Safety and evidence

### Is Remedy physical therapy?

No. Remedy is a fitness app. It does not diagnose or treat conditions and is not a substitute for a doctor or physical therapist.

### Is Remedy safe to use with back pain?

For everyday back pain in people with no warning signs, exercise is one of the most recommended options in clinical guidelines. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain or pain spreading down a leg, and see a clinician if you have [warning signs](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/when-to-see-a-doctor-for-back-pain).

### Is Remedy backed by research?

The approach, a progressive program of mobility, stability, and strength exercise, follows what guidelines like NICE and the American College of Physicians recommend for low back pain. Remedy has not run its own clinical trial of the app. Our guides link to every source.

### Who writes the guides?

The Remedy team. Guides are general fitness information based on published clinical guidelines and research, and every claim links to its source. They are not written or reviewed by a clinician. See our [editorial standards](https://remedyrecoveries.com/about#editorial).

## Your armadillo

### What is the armadillo?

Every Remedy account comes with one armadillo that you name. It shows how many sessions you have finished. It is not a comment on your back, and it is not a promise about pain.

### When does the armadillo move up?

It has five stages. Curled is 0 finished sessions. It moves up at 1, 4, 9, and 15 finished sessions, the 1st, 4th, 9th, and 15th. Missed days do not shrink it. It does not describe your back.

### What does the armadillo do all day?

It stays at the stage you have reached. It does not describe your back.

## Account and data

### What data does Remedy collect?

Your onboarding answers, session history, and pain check-ins, so the app can build and adjust your program. The [Privacy Policy](https://remedyrecoveries.com/privacy) has the full details.

### How do I delete my account?

In the app, go to Profile and choose Delete Account, or [email us](https://remedyrecoveries.com/contact).

### How do I contact Remedy?

Email [social@remedyrecoveries.com](mailto:social@remedyrecoveries.com).

# About Remedy

Remedy makes a back pain app for iPhone. It is a program of short sessions, with a video on every exercise.

A fitness program, not medical care.

## What we make

Remedy: Back Pain Relief is an iPhone app. You answer a short onboarding about your back. It builds a 10 to 16 week program. Sessions are 15, 20, or 30 minutes, on 3 to 7 days you pick. You rate pain before the session and after it. You also name an armadillo. It moves up at 1, 4, 9, and 15 finished sessions, and missed days do not shrink it. It does not describe your back. It launched on the App Store on October 13, 2026.

- **What it is:** Back fitness app for people with back pain

- **Platform:** iPhone, iOS 15.1 or later

- **Program length:** 10 to 16 weeks, set by how long your back has hurt and how it behaves

- **Sessions:** You pick 3 to 7 days a week

- **Exercises:** A demonstration video for every exercise

- **Price:** Free to download. $4.99/week, $12.99/month, or $79.99/year

- **Free trial:** 7 days weekly, 14 days monthly, and 7 days annual, where offered

- **Age:** 17+

- **Made by:** Kumar Holdings LLC, d/b/a Remedy

- **Released:** October 13, 2026

## Why it exists

People with a sore back often save a few videos and stop. Or they pay for care they cannot keep up with.

Guidelines often recommend exercise for everyday back pain. It takes weeks, and it should get harder at a steady pace.

Remedy is that program. One session at a time. The armadillo is there so the next session is easier to start. It does not talk about your back.

## Who builds it

### Rahul Kumar

Founder and developer

Rahul studies computer engineering and computer science at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and competes in powerlifting. He built Remedy end to end: the iOS app, the program engine that turns onboarding answers into a plan, and subscriptions. He also co-founded [Relentless](https://relentlesstough.com/), a mental training app for athletes.

## How we write our guides

- Guides are general fitness information, not medical advice.

- Every factual claim about back pain links to its source: clinical guidelines such as NICE, the American College of Physicians, and the WHO, public health sites such as the NHS and MedlinePlus, and peer-reviewed research such as Cochrane reviews.

- Guides are written by the Remedy team. They are not written or reviewed by a clinician, and we say so rather than imply otherwise.

- Every guide includes the warning signs that mean you should see someone instead of using an app.

- When we compare Remedy with other options, we say that we make Remedy.

- We update guides when guidance changes. Each one shows when it was last updated. Spot a mistake? [Tell us](mailto:social@remedyrecoveries.com?subject=Guide%20correction).

Every exercise in the Remedy app, with how to do it, form cues, common mistakes, and where it fits in a back program. General fitness information, not medical advice.

## Mobility

Move the spine and hips through a comfortable range. Remedy uses these to warm up.

### Cat-cow stretch

An all-fours movement that alternates rounding and arching your spine.

### Hip flexor stretch

A lunge-position stretch for the front of the hip.

### McKenzie press-up

A press-up from lying on your stomach where the hips stay on the floor and the lower back extends.

## Core and stability

Hold the trunk steady while arms and legs move. The base everything else sits on.

[Core and stability

### Dead bug exercise

A core exercise done on your back: you slowly lower an opposite arm and leg while keeping your trunk still.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dead-bug)
[Core and stability

### Bird dog exercise

From your hands and knees, you reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your back still.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog)
[Core and stability

### Side plank from the knees

A shorter-lever side plank with your knees on the floor.
No equipment · Intermediate](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank-knees)
[Core and stability

### Side plank

A side plank on your feet.
No equipment · Advanced](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank)
[Core and stability

### Suitcase carry

Walking while holding a weight in one hand, like carrying a suitcase.
Band or dumbbells · Advanced](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/suitcase-carry)

## Glutes and hips

Hip extension strength, so the hips do the lifting instead of the low back.

### Glute bridge

Lying on your back with knees bent, you drive through your heels to lift your hips.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/glute-bridge)
[Glutes and hips

### Single-leg glute bridge

A glute bridge on one leg, with the other leg held straight.
No equipment · Intermediate](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/single-leg-glute-bridge)
[Glutes and hips

### Barbell hip thrust

A loaded bridge with your upper back on a bench and a barbell across your hips.
Gym · Advanced](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/barbell-hip-thrust)

## How to use this library

Pick a few exercises from different groups rather than many from one. A useful routine covers mobility, core stability, and strength. [Exercises for lower back pain](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/lower-back-pain-exercises) has a ready-made starter routine, and [core exercises for back pain](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/core-exercises-for-back-pain) shows how the stability exercises progress.

If you would rather not assemble it yourself, Remedy picks from this library for you based on your answers, sets the reps, and moves you to harder versions as you go.

# Cat-cow stretch

An all-fours movement that alternates rounding and arching your spine. It is one of the gentlest ways to get a stiff back moving, which is why Remedy often uses it at the start of a session.

Also called: cat-camel, cat cow pose

- **Type:** Mobility

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 sets of 10 slow reps

## How to do it

- Start on your hands and knees, hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
- Breathe in as you let your belly drop and lift your chest and tailbone, arching your back (cow).
- Breathe out as you push the floor away and round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat).
- Move slowly between the two positions, staying in a range that feels comfortable.

## Form cues

- Inhale and arch; exhale and round.
- Let your head follow your spine.

## Common mistakes

- Rushing. Two or three seconds each way is about right.
- Forcing the end range. It should feel like movement, not a stretch you have to push into.
- Bending only at the neck. Try to move from the tailbone up.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** If kneeling is uncomfortable, put a folded towel under your knees, or do a seated version: hands on your thighs, round and arch from a chair.

## Why it helps a sore back

It moves every segment of the spine through flexion and extension without load, so it works as a warm-up and as a way to loosen up first thing in the morning.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Cat-Cow Stretch**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by mornings or after rest or sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 2 sets of 10 slow reps, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

Cat-cow stretch in the Remedy app

Get it in a program

Remedy builds this into a 10 to 16 week plan with video, sets, and reps.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/open-book-rotation">
# Open-book rotation

A side-lying rotation for the upper and middle back. The top arm opens like the cover of a book while the knees stay stacked.

Also called: open book stretch, thoracic rotation

- **Type:** Mobility

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Upper and mid back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 sets of 8 per side

## How to do it

- Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent to about 90 degrees, one knee on top of the other.
- Reach both arms straight out in front of you, palms together.
- Keeping your knees together, lift the top arm and open it across your body toward the floor behind you.
- Let your eyes follow your hand. Pause, then bring the arm back to the start.
- Finish your reps, then roll over and do the other side.

## Form cues

- Keep both knees stacked.
- Open the top arm and let your eyes follow your hand.

## Common mistakes

- Letting the top knee slide back. That moves the rotation into the low back.
- Forcing the arm to the floor. Go as far as is comfortable.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** A pillow under your head and between your knees makes the position easier to hold.

## Why it helps a sore back

Most daily rotation should come from the upper back rather than the lower back. This trains that rotation in a supported position, which makes it a common choice for people who sit a lot.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Open-Book Rotation**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long or mornings or after rest. A typical starting dose is 2 sets of 8 per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/thoracic-extension">
# Chair thoracic extension

A gentle backward bend of the upper back over the top of a chair. You can do it at a desk in under a minute.

Also called: seated thoracic extension, upper back extension over chair

- **Type:** Mobility

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Upper and mid back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 sets of 8

## How to do it

- Sit tall in a chair with a firm back that reaches about the bottom of your shoulder blades.
- Put your hands behind your head and bring your elbows in a little.
- Lean back over the top edge of the chair, letting your upper back extend.
- Pause for a breath, then return to sitting tall.

## Form cues

- Hands behind your head.
- Arch only the upper back over the chair, not the low back.

## Common mistakes

- Pushing the ribs and belly forward, which turns it into a low back arch.
- Pulling on the head with the hands.

## Easier and harder versions

- Remedy keeps this one steady and changes the work around it instead.

## Why it helps a sore back

Long stretches of sitting and looking at a screen keep the upper back rounded. This moves it the other way, using the chair back as a pivot so the bend comes from the upper back and not the lower back.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Thoracic Extension (Chair-Assisted)**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 2 sets of 8, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/hip-flexor-stretch">
# Hip flexor stretch

A lunge-position stretch for the front of the hip. Remedy’s version starts half-kneeling, with one knee on the floor.

Also called: half-kneeling hip flexor stretch, kneeling lunge stretch

- **Type:** Mobility

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 holds of 30 seconds per side

## How to do it

- Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front of you, both knees at about 90 degrees.
- Stand your spine up tall.
- Tuck the hip of the back leg under, as if pointing your tailbone down.
- Keeping that tuck, shift your weight forward slowly until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
- Hold, breathing normally, then switch sides.

## Form cues

- Tall spine.
- Tuck the back hip under, then shift forward until the front of that hip stretches.

## Common mistakes

- Arching the low back to get further forward. The tuck matters more than the distance.
- Leaning the torso forward.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** If kneeling hurts your knee, pad it with a cushion, or do the same stretch standing in a split stance with a hand on a wall.

## Why it helps a sore back

The hip flexors attach to the lower spine and pelvis, and they spend most of a sitting day in a shortened position. Stretching them is a common part of back routines for people who sit.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Standing Hip Flexor Stretch**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long or standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 2 holds of 30 seconds per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/mckenzie-press-up">
# McKenzie press-up

A press-up from lying on your stomach where the hips stay on the floor and the lower back extends. It comes from the McKenzie method, also called Mechanical Diagnosis and Therapy.

Also called: prone press-up, cobra press-up for back, lumbar extension press-up

- **Type:** Mobility

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10

## How to do it

- Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders, like the bottom of a push-up.
- Relax your hips, buttocks, and legs completely.
- Press through your hands to lift your chest, letting your low back sag while your hips stay on the floor.
- Straighten your arms as far as is comfortable and pause.
- Lower slowly back down.

## Form cues

- Hips stay on the floor.
- Press the chest up fully, pause, then lower slowly.

## Common mistakes

- Squeezing the glutes, which stops the low back from extending.
- Letting the hips lift off the floor.

Stop if
Stop if pain spreads further into your buttock or down your leg, or if you get numbness or tingling. Pain moving away from the spine is a sign this movement is not right for you right now.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** Start by resting on your forearms (lying on elbows) for 30 seconds to a minute before trying full press-ups.

## Why it helps a sore back

Some people with low back pain find that repeated backward bending eases their symptoms, especially when sitting and bending are what bother them. It is also one of the exercises where how your body responds matters most, so watch where you feel it.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **McKenzie Press-Up**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long or bending or lifting or standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

# Dead bug exercise

A core exercise done on your back: you slowly lower an opposite arm and leg while keeping your trunk still. It trains your core to hold steady while your limbs move.

Also called: dead bugs, dying bug

- **Type:** Core and stability

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Beginner

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10

## How to do it

- Lie on your back with your arms pointing at the ceiling and your hips and knees bent to 90 degrees.
- Gently brace your stomach, as if getting ready for a light poke in the belly.
- Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor over about three seconds.
- Stop before your low back starts to lift off the floor, then return to the start.
- Repeat on the other side. Each side counts as one rep.

## Form cues

- Lower opposite arm and leg over 3 seconds.
- If the low back lifts, use a smaller range.

## Common mistakes

- Moving fast. Slow is the whole point.
- Holding your breath. Breathe out as the limbs lower.
- Letting the low back arch away from the floor.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** Move only the legs, tapping one heel to the floor at a time, before adding the arms.

- **Harder:** [Bird dog exercise](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog)

## Why it helps a sore back

Holding the spine steady while the arms and legs move is the job your core does all day. The dead bug trains it with the floor supporting you, so it is a common early step in back programs.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Dead Bug**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog">
# Bird dog exercise

From your hands and knees, you reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your back still. It is one of the most widely used exercises for back stability.

Also called: bird dogs, quadruped opposite arm leg raise

- **Type:** Core and stability

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Beginner

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 5 per side, holding each rep for 10 seconds

## How to do it

- Start on your hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips, with a flat back.
- Gently brace your stomach.
- Slide one leg back and lift it to hip height while reaching the opposite arm forward to shoulder height.
- Hold for about ten seconds, keeping your hips level and your back still.
- Lower with control and switch sides.

## Form cues

- Reach opposite arm and leg.
- Keep the back still and the hips level.

## Common mistakes

- Lifting the leg too high, which arches the low back.
- Rotating the hips open. Imagine balancing a cup of water on your lower back.
- Rushing between sides.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Dead bug exercise](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dead-bug)

- **To make it easier:** Move only the arms first, then only the legs, before combining them.

- **Harder:** [Side plank from the knees](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank-knees)

## Why it helps a sore back

It trains the muscles along the spine and around the trunk to keep the back steady while the hips and shoulders move. Remedy uses short holds of about ten seconds, repeated, which tend to work better than one long shaky hold.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Bird Dog**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting or standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 5 per side, holding each rep for 10 seconds, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

Bird dog exercise in the Remedy app

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank-knees">
# Side plank from the knees

A shorter-lever side plank with your knees on the floor. It builds endurance in the muscles on the side of the trunk.

Also called: modified side plank, kneeling side plank

- **Type:** Core and stability

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 4 holds of 10 seconds per side

## How to do it

- Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your knees bent behind you.
- Stack your hips and shoulders.
- Lift your hips until your ear, shoulder, hip, and knee form a straight line.
- Hold for about ten seconds, breathing normally, then lower.
- Do your holds, then switch sides.

## Form cues

- Lift the hips so ear, shoulder, hip, and knee line up.
- Don’t let the hips sag.

## Common mistakes

- Letting the top hip roll forward or back.
- Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear. Push the floor away.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Bird dog exercise](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog)

- **Harder:** [Side plank](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank)

## Why it helps a sore back

The side of the trunk keeps you upright when you carry something in one hand or walk on uneven ground. Starting from the knees lets you build that endurance before taking the full plank.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Side Plank (Knees)**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 4 holds of 10 seconds per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank">
# Side plank

A side plank on your feet. Your body holds a straight line from ankles to shoulders, supported on one forearm.

Also called: full side plank, side bridge

- **Type:** Core and stability

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 4 holds of 10 seconds per side

## How to do it

- Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs straight, feet stacked or staggered.
- Brace gently and lift your hips off the floor.
- Hold a straight line from your ankles to your shoulders for about ten seconds.
- Lower with control. Do your holds, then switch sides.

## Form cues

- Straight line from ankles to shoulders.
- Lift the hips; don’t sag or pike.

## Common mistakes

- Hips dropping toward the floor as you tire. End the hold when form goes.
- Piking the hips up and back.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Side plank from the knees](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank-knees)

- **To make it easier:** Stagger your feet, top foot in front, for a wider base.

- **Harder:** [Suitcase carry](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/suitcase-carry)

## Why it helps a sore back

It is the progression of the kneeling side plank and one of the standard exercises for side-of-trunk endurance. Remedy moves you here once the kneeling version feels steady.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Side Plank (Full)**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by standing or walking or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 4 holds of 10 seconds per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/suitcase-carry">
# Suitcase carry

Walking while holding a weight in one hand, like carrying a suitcase. The goal is to stay upright and not lean.

Also called: single-arm farmer carry, one-arm farmers walk

- **Type:** Core and stability

- **Equipment:** Band or dumbbells

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 carries of 30 seconds per side

## How to do it

- Pick up a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand using a hip hinge, not by rounding your back.
- Stand tall with your shoulders level and the weight by your side.
- Walk at a normal pace for about 30 seconds, keeping your trunk upright.
- Set the weight down with the same hinge, switch hands, and repeat.

## Form cues

- Walk tall.
- Keep both shoulders level; don’t lean toward or away from the weight.

## Common mistakes

- Leaning away from the weight to balance it.
- Shrugging the loaded shoulder up.
- Starting too heavy. Choose a weight you can carry with good posture the whole time.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Side plank](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank)

## Why it helps a sore back

Carrying something on one side tries to bend you sideways. Resisting that is exactly what the side-of-trunk muscles do in daily life, from grocery bags to a child on one hip.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Suitcase Carry**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by standing or walking or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 carries of 30 seconds per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/glute-bridge">
# Glute bridge

Lying on your back with knees bent, you drive through your heels to lift your hips. It strengthens the glutes, the main muscles that extend the hips.

Also called: hip bridge, bridge exercise

- **Type:** Glutes and hips

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Beginner

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12

## How to do it

- Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, about hip-width apart.
- Rest your arms by your sides.
- Push through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your shoulders, hips, and knees line up.
- Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

## Form cues

- Drive through your heels and squeeze.
- Keep the ribs down; don’t arch the low back.

## Common mistakes

- Pushing the hips too high and arching the low back.
- Feeling it mostly in the hamstrings. Bring your feet a little closer to your hips.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Harder:** [Single-leg glute bridge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/single-leg-glute-bridge)

## Why it helps a sore back

Strong glutes take load off the low back when you lift, stand up, or climb stairs. The bridge is a simple, well-supported way to start building them.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Glute Bridge**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long or standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

Glute bridge in the Remedy app

Remedy builds this into a 10 to 16 week plan with video, sets, and reps.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/single-leg-glute-bridge">
# Single-leg glute bridge

A glute bridge on one leg, with the other leg held straight. It doubles the load on the working side and adds a balance challenge for the hips.

Also called: one-leg bridge, single leg hip bridge

- **Type:** Glutes and hips

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10 per side

## How to do it

- Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
- Straighten one leg so it lines up with the other thigh.
- Drive through the heel of the planted foot to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
- Keep both hips level at the top, then lower slowly.
- Finish your reps and switch legs.

## Form cues

- Drive through the planted heel.
- Keep both hips level at the top; don’t let one drop.

## Common mistakes

- The hip on the lifted-leg side dropping.
- Arching the low back to get height.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Glute bridge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/glute-bridge)

- **Harder:** [Barbell hip thrust](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/barbell-hip-thrust)

## Why it helps a sore back

In Remedy it is the step up from the two-leg bridge: instead of piling on more reps, the program moves you to a harder version.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Single-Leg Glute Bridge**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by standing or walking or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10 per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/barbell-hip-thrust">
# Barbell hip thrust

A loaded bridge with your upper back on a bench and a barbell across your hips. It lets you load the glutes heavily without putting the weight on your spine.

Also called: hip thrust, weighted hip thrust

- **Type:** Glutes and hips

- **Equipment:** Gym

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Sit on the floor with your upper back against the side of a bench and a padded barbell over your hips.
- Bend your knees and plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart.
- Drive through your heels to lift your hips until they lock out and your shins are vertical.
- Keep your chin tucked and ribs down at the top, then lower under control.

## Form cues

- Drive the hips up until they lock out.
- Don’t arch the low back.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Finishing the rep by arching the low back instead of extending the hips.
- Feet too far forward, which shifts the work to the hamstrings.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Single-leg glute bridge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/single-leg-glute-bridge)

## Why it helps a sore back

For people who train in a gym, it is a way to keep building hip strength with real load while the low back stays out of the heavy lifting.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Barbell Hip Thrust**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by working out or sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge">
# Hip hinge

Bending forward by pushing your hips back while your spine stays long. It is the movement pattern behind deadlifts and behind picking things up safely.

Also called: hip hinge exercise, how to hip hinge

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Beginner

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12

## How to do it

- Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees softly bent.
- Put your hands on the front of your hips.
- Push your hips straight back, letting your chest come forward while your back stays long.
- Go until you feel your hamstrings stretch, then stand up by driving your hips forward.

## Form cues

- Push the hips back, not the knees forward.
- Keep a long back and soft knees.

## Common mistakes

- Bending from the waist and rounding the back.
- Turning it into a squat by bending the knees too much.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** Hold a broomstick along your back, touching your head, upper back, and tailbone. If any point loses contact, you are rounding.

- **Harder:** [Banded Romanian deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/banded-romanian-deadlift) or [Single-leg Romanian deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/single-leg-romanian-deadlift)

## Why it helps a sore back

Learning to bend from the hips is one of the most useful things a person with a sore back can practice, because it is how you pick things up every day. Remedy uses it to build the pattern before adding load.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Bodyweight Hip Hinge**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/banded-romanian-deadlift">
# Banded Romanian deadlift

A hip hinge against a resistance band anchored under your feet. The band adds load at the top of the movement without heavy weight.

Also called: resistance band RDL, band deadlift

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Band or dumbbells

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Stand on the middle of a resistance band with your feet hip-width apart, holding the ends.
- Stand tall with soft knees.
- Hinge at the hips, sliding your hands down your thighs while your back stays long.
- When you feel your hamstrings, drive your hips forward to stand against the band.

## Form cues

- Hinge at the hips, not the waist.
- Feel the hamstrings, then stand.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Rounding the back to reach lower.
- Leaning back at the top.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Hip hinge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge)

- **Harder:** [Dumbbell Romanian deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dumbbell-romanian-deadlift)

## Why it helps a sore back

It is the first loaded step after the bodyweight hinge in Remedy, and a good option at home.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Banded Romanian Deadlift**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

# Single-leg Romanian deadlift

A hip hinge on one leg while the other leg reaches straight back. It builds strength in the back of the hips and legs and challenges balance.

Also called: single leg RDL, single leg deadlift bodyweight

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 8 per side

## How to do it

- Stand on one leg with a soft knee. Hold a wall or chair for balance if you need it.
- Hinge forward at the hip while the free leg reaches straight back.
- Keep your back long and your hips square to the floor.
- When you feel the hamstring of the standing leg, drive back up to standing.
- Finish your reps and switch legs.

## Form cues

- Hinge at the hip, not the waist.
- The free leg reaches straight back; keep the back long.

## Common mistakes

- Opening the hip of the free leg toward the ceiling.
- Rounding the back to get the hands lower.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Hip hinge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge)

- **Harder:** [Dumbbell Romanian deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dumbbell-romanian-deadlift)

## Why it helps a sore back

It loads one hip at a time with no equipment, which makes it a useful step up for people training at home.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 8 per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dumbbell-romanian-deadlift">
# Dumbbell Romanian deadlift

A hip hinge holding a dumbbell in each hand. A slow lower builds strength through the hamstrings, glutes, and the muscles along the spine.

Also called: dumbbell RDL, DB RDL

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Band or dumbbells

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10, lowering over 3 seconds

## How to do it

- Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
- Soften your knees and hinge at the hips, sliding the weights down close to your legs.
- Take about three seconds to lower, keeping your back long.
- When you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually around mid-shin, drive your hips forward to stand.

## Form cues

- Hinge with a long back.
- Lower for 3 seconds, then stand.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Letting the dumbbells drift away from your legs.
- Rounding the back at the bottom to go lower.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Banded Romanian deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/banded-romanian-deadlift)

- **Harder:** [Kettlebell deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/kettlebell-deadlift)

## Why it helps a sore back

It is one of the main loaded hinges in Remedy’s later weeks for people with dumbbells.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10, lowering over 3 seconds, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/kettlebell-deadlift">
# Kettlebell deadlift

Lifting a kettlebell from the floor between your feet using a hip hinge. It is how you learn to pick something heavy up off the ground.

Also called: KB deadlift, kettlebell deadlift form

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Gym

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 8, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Stand with the kettlebell on the floor between your feet, in line with your heels or mid-foot.
- Hinge your hips back and bend your knees enough to grip the handle with a flat back.
- Brace, then stand up by driving your hips forward until you are tall.
- Hinge back down the same way and set the bell down with control.

## Form cues

- Hinge, grip, stand by driving the hips forward.
- Keep a flat back.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Squatting down with the chest dropping, or rounding over to reach the bell.
- Leaning back at the top.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Dumbbell Romanian deadlift](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dumbbell-romanian-deadlift) or [Hip hinge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge)

## Why it helps a sore back

Picking things up off the floor is one of the moments people worry about most with a sore back. Practicing it with a manageable load builds confidence and strength for it.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Kettlebell Deadlift**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting or working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 8, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-squat">
# Bodyweight squat

A controlled squat with no load. It builds leg and hip strength for getting up from chairs, the floor, and the car.

Also called: air squat, squat for beginners

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Beginner

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12

## How to do it

- Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
- Sit your hips back and down while keeping your chest tall.
- Go as low as is comfortable with your weight in the middle of your feet.
- Push through your feet to stand back up.

## Form cues

- Sit the hips back, chest tall, weight in mid-foot.
- Knees track over the toes.

## Common mistakes

- Knees caving inward.
- Heels lifting off the floor.
- Dropping fast to the bottom.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** Squat down to a chair and stand back up. Lower the seat height over time.

- **Harder:** [Goblet squat](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/goblet-squat) or [Split squat](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/split-squat)

## Why it helps a sore back

Strong legs share the work of lifting and standing so the back does less of it. Remedy uses the bodyweight squat before adding a dumbbell.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Bodyweight Squat**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by working out or bending or lifting. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

Bodyweight squat in the Remedy app

Remedy builds this into a 10 to 16 week plan with video, sets, and reps.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/goblet-squat">
# Goblet squat

A squat holding one dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest. The weight in front helps you stay upright.

Also called: dumbbell goblet squat, kettlebell goblet squat

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Band or dumbbells

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands under the top end.
- Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
- Squat down between your knees, keeping your chest tall and elbows inside your knees.
- Drive up through your feet to stand.

## Form cues

- Chest tall, elbows inside the knees.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Letting the weight pull you forward.
- Rounding the low back at the bottom. Stop above the point where it tucks.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Bodyweight squat](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-squat)

- **Harder:** [Leg press](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/leg-press)

## Why it helps a sore back

Holding the weight in front counterbalances you, which makes it easier to keep the chest tall than a barbell squat. It is Remedy’s first loaded squat.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Goblet Squat**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by working out or standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/split-squat">
# Split squat

A squat in a staggered stance, one foot forward and one back. It trains one leg at a time.

Also called: static lunge, split squat form

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10 per side, lowering over 3 seconds

## How to do it

- Stand in a long stagger, one foot forward and the back heel lifted.
- Keep your torso tall and your weight mostly on the front foot.
- Lower your back knee straight down toward the floor over about three seconds.
- Drive through the front heel to come back up.
- Finish your reps and switch legs.

## Form cues

- Torso tall.
- Lower the back knee straight down over 3 seconds, then drive through the front heel.

## Common mistakes

- Feet in one line like a tightrope. Keep them about hip-width apart side to side.
- Pushing off the back foot instead of the front heel.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Bodyweight squat](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-squat)

- **To make it easier:** Hold a wall or chair for balance, and go only part of the way down.

## Why it helps a sore back

Single-leg strength helps with stairs, walking, and getting up from the floor, and the split squat builds it without any equipment.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Split Squat**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by working out or standing or walking. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10 per side, lowering over 3 seconds, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/leg-press">
# Leg press

A machine press for the legs. Your back is supported by the seat while the legs push the load.

Also called: leg press machine, leg press with back pain

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Gym

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Sit in the machine with your back and hips flat against the pad.
- Place your feet flat on the platform about hip-width apart.
- Release the safety and lower the platform under control until your knees are bent, stopping before your low back peels off the pad.
- Push through the middle of your feet to straighten your legs without locking your knees.

## Form cues

- Feet flat, push through mid-foot.
- Don’t let the low back curl at the bottom.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Going so deep the hips roll up and the low back rounds off the pad.
- Locking the knees hard at the top.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Goblet squat](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/goblet-squat)

## Why it helps a sore back

It lets you load the legs heavily while the seat supports your back, which is useful for gym-goers training around a sore back.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Leg Press**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by working out. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

# Resistance band row

Pulling a resistance band toward your lower ribs and squeezing your shoulder blades together. It strengthens the upper and middle back.

Also called: band row, seated band row

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Band or dumbbells

- **Area:** Upper and mid back

- **Level:** Beginner

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Anchor a band at chest height, or sit with legs straight and loop it around your feet.
- Hold the ends with your arms straight in front of you and sit or stand tall.
- Pull your elbows back toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
- Pause, then let your arms straighten slowly.

## Form cues

- Pull to the lower ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
- Leaning back to finish the pull.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Harder:** [Seated cable row](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/seated-cable-row)

## Why it helps a sore back

Upper back strength helps you sit and stand tall without effort. Rows are Remedy’s main strength work for upper and mid back discomfort.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Banded Row**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/seated-cable-row">
# Seated cable row

A seated horizontal pull on a cable machine. It builds the muscles between and around the shoulder blades.

Also called: cable row, low row machine

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Gym

- **Area:** Upper and mid back

- **Level:** Intermediate

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard

## How to do it

- Sit at the cable row station with your feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
- Grip the handle and sit tall with your arms straight.
- Pull the handle to your stomach by squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your torso still.
- Let the weight back out slowly until your arms are straight.

## Form cues

- Sit tall.
- Pull by squeezing the shoulder blades; don’t lean back.
- The last two reps should feel hard.

## Common mistakes

- Rocking the torso back and forth to move the weight.
- Rounding forward at the end of each rep.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Resistance band row](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/banded-row)

## Why it helps a sore back

It is the gym version of the band row, with load you can increase in small steps.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Seated Cable Row**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 12, last two reps hard, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/back-extension">
# 45-degree back extension

A hinge on a 45-degree bench with your hips on the pad and feet anchored. You lower your upper body, then rise until your body is one straight line.

Also called: hyperextension, roman chair back extension

- **Type:** Strength

- **Equipment:** Gym

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Advanced

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 3 sets of 10

## How to do it

- Set the pad so it sits just below your hip bones and lock your heels under the foot pads.
- Start with your body in a straight line and your arms crossed on your chest.
- Hinge at the hips to lower your upper body toward the floor with a long back.
- Rise by squeezing your glutes until your body is one straight line again.

## Form cues

- Hinge down, then rise until the body is one line.
- Stop at straight; don’t arch past it.

## Common mistakes

- Arching back past a straight line at the top.
- Pad set too high, so you bend at the waist instead of the hips.

## Easier and harder versions

- **Easier:** [Hip hinge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge)

## Why it helps a sore back

It strengthens the glutes, hamstrings, and muscles along the spine together. Remedy places it late in a program, after the bodyweight hinge feels solid.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Back Extension (45°)**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by bending or lifting or sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 3 sets of 10, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

# Child’s pose for back pain

A resting stretch where you sit back toward your heels with your arms stretched out in front. It eases the low back and hips at the end of a session.

Also called: child pose stretch, balasana

- **Type:** Stretches and recovery

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 holds of 40 seconds

## How to do it

- Kneel with your big toes together and your knees apart.
- Sit your hips back toward your heels.
- Walk your hands forward and rest your forehead on the floor or a cushion.
- Breathe slowly into your back and sides and hold.

## Form cues

- Sit back toward your heels, arms long, forehead down.
- Breathe into the stretch.

## Common mistakes

- Forcing the hips down to the heels. Go as far as is comfortable.

## Easier and harder versions

- **To make it easier:** Put a pillow between your heels and hips, or under your chest, if you cannot sit all the way back.

## Why it helps a sore back

It is an easy, supported position to finish a session in, and a common way to wind down the low back after strength work.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Child’s Pose Hold**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by mornings or after rest. A typical starting dose is 2 holds of 40 seconds, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

Child’s pose for back pain in the Remedy app

Get it in a program

Remedy builds this into a 10 to 16 week plan with video, sets, and reps.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/figure-4-stretch">
# Figure-4 stretch

A stretch for the glutes and the piriformis, done lying on your back with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee.

Also called: figure four stretch, supine piriformis stretch, glute stretch lying down

- **Type:** Stretches and recovery

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 holds of 30 seconds per side

## How to do it

- Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
- Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
- Reach through and hold behind the thigh of the uncrossed leg.
- Gently pull that thigh toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the buttock of the crossed leg.
- Hold, then switch sides.

## Form cues

- Cross ankle over opposite knee.
- Gently pull the uncrossed thigh toward you.

## Common mistakes

- Lifting the head and shoulders off the floor. Use a strap or towel if you cannot reach.

## Easier and harder versions

- Remedy keeps this one steady and changes the work around it instead.

## Why it helps a sore back

Tight glutes are a common complaint alongside low back stiffness, and this stretch reaches them without loading the back.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Supine Figure-4 Stretch**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long. A typical starting dose is 2 holds of 30 seconds per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

<page url="https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/hamstring-stretch">
# Lying hamstring stretch

A hamstring stretch done lying on your back, holding behind your thigh and straightening the knee.

Also called: supine hamstring stretch, hamstring stretch for lower back

- **Type:** Stretches and recovery

- **Equipment:** No equipment

- **Area:** Lower back

- **Level:** Gentle

- **Starting dose in Remedy:** 2 holds of 30 seconds per side

## How to do it

- Lie on your back with both knees bent.
- Lift one leg and hold behind the thigh with both hands, or loop a towel around the foot.
- Slowly straighten the knee until you feel a pull in the back of the thigh.
- Hold, breathing normally, then switch legs.

## Form cues

- Hold behind the thigh and straighten the knee until you feel a pull, not a burn.

## Common mistakes

- Pulling the leg so far the hips lift off the floor.
- Bouncing into the stretch.

Stop if
If the stretch causes tingling or shooting pain down the leg, ease off. That is a nerve-related feeling, not a hamstring stretch.

## Easier and harder versions

- Remedy keeps this one steady and changes the work around it instead.

## Why it helps a sore back

Lying down keeps your back supported while you stretch, which is kinder to a sore back than bending forward to touch your toes.

## How Remedy uses it

In the app it is called **Supine Hamstring Stretch**. Remedy is more likely to pick it if you say your back is bothered by sitting too long or mornings or after rest. A typical starting dose is 2 holds of 30 seconds per side, and the program adjusts reps as the weeks go on. Every exercise in the app has a demonstration video.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, or pain, numbness, or tingling spreading down a leg.

A resting stretch where you sit back toward your heels with your arms stretched out in front.
No equipment · Gentle](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/childs-pose)

### Figure-4 stretch

A stretch for the glutes and the piriformis, done lying on your back with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee.
No equipment · Gentle](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/figure-4-stretch)

# Exercises for lower back pain: what actually helps

Exercise is one of the most recommended things you can do for a sore lower back. There is no single magic move. What works is a sensible mix, done regularly and made a little harder over time.

By [the Remedy team](https://remedyrecoveries.com/about#editorial) · Published October 23, 2026 · 3 min read · 7 sources

On this page

- [Does exercise help lower back pain?](#does-exercise-help)
- [Which exercises are best?](#which-exercises)
- [A simple starter routine](#starter-routine)
- [What should I avoid?](#what-to-avoid)
- [How Remedy fits](#how-remedy-fits)
- [Questions](#questions)
- [Sources](#sources)

Key takeaways

- Clinical guidelines from the UK, US, and WHO all list exercise as a first-line option for low back pain.
- No single exercise is best. Several types help, and the one you will keep doing beats the perfect one you skip.
- A good routine covers mobility, core stability, and hip and back strength, and gets harder over the weeks.

## Does exercise help lower back pain?

Yes, for most people. Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide, and in most cases there is no single structural cause that a scan would find [1]. That is part of why guidelines lean so heavily on exercise and staying active rather than on fixing one specific thing.

The UK’s NICE guideline recommends exercise programs for managing low back pain [2]. The American College of Physicians recommends exercise, along with other non-drug options like yoga and tai chi, as a first step for chronic low back pain [3]. The World Health Organization’s 2023 guideline also lists structured exercise programs among its recommended options [4].

A Cochrane review of 249 trials found that exercise probably reduces pain for people with chronic low back pain compared with no treatment or usual care [5]. The average effect is moderate, not miraculous, which is a good reason to treat it as a habit you build over weeks rather than a one-off fix.

## Which exercises are best?

A large network meta-analysis compared different exercise types for chronic low back pain. It found benefits across several, including Pilates, stability (motor control) training, resistance training, and aerobic exercise [6]. In practice that means the label matters less than covering a few bases:

- **Mobility.** Moving the spine and hips through a comfortable range. [Cat-cow stretch](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/cat-cow), [open-book rotation](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/open-book-rotation), and a [hip flexor stretch](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/hip-flexor-stretch) are common choices.

- **Core stability.** Holding the trunk steady while arms and legs move: the [bird dog](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog), [dead bug](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dead-bug), and [side plank from the knees](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/side-plank-knees).

- **Hip and back strength.** The muscles that do the work when you lift and stand up: [glute bridge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/glute-bridge), [hip hinge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge), and [bodyweight squat](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-squat).

- **General activity.** Walking counts. [Walking for back pain](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/is-walking-good-for-back-pain) has its own guide.

## A simple starter routine

This is the kind of session Remedy builds early in a program for someone with no equipment. It takes about 15 minutes. Move slowly and stay in a range that feels manageable.

- **[Cat-cow stretch](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/cat-cow)**: 2 sets of 10 slow reps to warm up.

- **[Bird dog](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog)**: 3 sets of 5 per side, holding each for about 10 seconds.

- **[Dead bug](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dead-bug)**: 3 sets of 10, lowering over about 3 seconds.

- **[Glute bridge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/glute-bridge)**: 3 sets of 12.

- **[Hip hinge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge)**: 3 sets of 12.

- **[Child’s pose for back pain](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/childs-pose)**: 2 holds of about 40 seconds to cool down.

Do it three times a week. When a move feels easy for a full week, move to the harder version listed on its exercise page, for example from the glute bridge to the [single-leg glute bridge](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/single-leg-glute-bridge). That is how Remedy progresses: harder variants, not endless extra reps.

## What should I avoid?

You do not need to avoid bending or lifting forever. What helps is choosing a version you can do with control right now and building up from there. A few practical rules:

- Mild, general discomfort that settles within a day is common when you start. Sharp pain, or pain spreading down a leg, means stop that movement.

- Swap an exercise that always makes things worse for another in the same group.

- Don’t judge a routine after one week. [How long to stick with it](https://remedyrecoveries.com/guides/how-long-to-stick-with-a-back-routine) covers realistic timelines.

## How Remedy fits

Remedy builds this kind of program from a short onboarding, including where it hurts and what makes it worse. Every session has a warm-up, main work, and cooldown, every exercise has a demonstration video, and the difficulty climbs week by week. [See how it works](https://remedyrecoveries.com/how) or browse the [exercise guides](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/).

### Bird dog exercise

From your hands and knees, you reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your back still.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bird-dog)

A core exercise done on your back: you slowly lower an opposite arm and leg while keeping your trunk still.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/dead-bug)

Lying on your back with knees bent, you drive through your heels to lift your hips.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/glute-bridge)
[Strength

### Hip hinge

Bending forward by pushing your hips back while your spine stays long.
No equipment · Beginner](https://remedyrecoveries.com/exercises/bodyweight-hip-hinge)
